title: The Rough Trail
premise: Riverboat captain Sable Brightwater has spent nine years outrunning a name, jumping sandbars before debts, magistrates, or questions can catch up. When an extreme spring tide uncovers the Drowned Door — a cave legend says admits no one free — a dying salvager washes out with a chart to the Coronation, the steamer that went down carrying the deed to every toll on the river. Harbor-magnate Odile Vann brings her salvage fleet to claim it, and she alone knows who Sable used to be; the race is six tides before the dry season strands them all. Inside, where entry costs a memory apiece, Sable finds the deed signed with their own buried family name, burns it rather than become their father, and lets the sealing tide bury the past — walking out nameless, lighter, and finally willing to stop moving.
about_author: Bram Delacroix is the pen name of a former tidal-river deckhand who spent a decade writing shipping columns in port towns before going deliberately obscure. The Rough Trail draws on salvage divers' testimony, several of whom still refuse work above the upper bends.

chapters.title: The Door the River Opens
chapters.summary: Sable Brightwater pilots the Marguerite downriver, mooring shallow and leaving early, because stopping lets the past catch up. An extreme spring tide drains away to expose the Drowned Door, a sea cave legend says admits no one free. A drowning salvager washes out clutching a brass token and half a chart naming the Coronation — and the mark above the door matches the scar Sable can't explain. Inside Sable's head, restlessness cracks into dread; against their deckhand's pleas, they turn upstream.

chapters.title: A Name, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: The salvage fleet anchors across the channel, and its owner, Odile Vann, boards the Marguerite and greets Sable by a name nobody has spoken in nine years. She offers a share of the Coronation's treasure for piloting her dredges over the bar. With six usable tides left, Sable refuses, and reprisal follows — cut anchors, stolen charts, a bought deckhand. Told through Sable's eyes, the chapter runs on fear curdling into a stranger feeling: the relief of being recognized.

chapters.title: Admission
chapters.summary: On the fifth tide, seen through Sable's salt-stung eyes, the Marguerite threads the Door, and the cave collects admission: Pip forgets his mother's face, and Sable loses something they can't yet name. In the flooded hold they raise the deed, signed with Sable's buried family name — ownership of every toll on the river. Odile rises beside them, offering Sable's whole history back for the paper. Tempted to the bone, Sable burns it instead and hauls Pip out as Odile screams at the closing water.

chapters.title: Moorings
chapters.summary: The sixth tide arrives too weak, and the Door grinds shut for the year with the deed's ashes inside. Hunting for the reason they ran, Sable finds the cave took exactly that memory as its fee — and the loss lands like setting down heavy cargo. Speaking 'Brightwater' aloud as a chosen name rather than a hiding one, Sable moors deep for the dry season. Grief eases into belonging; when a dockside child asks about the cave, Sable pays the legend honestly: some things are worth the price of forgetting.
